text:
Colorado lost Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar less than a minute apart in Ottawa last Thursday, both to lower-body injuries, and found out Saturday that MacKinnon will miss about a month and Makar about two weeks. That is 30 points and 23 points gone from the lineup. The first answer was encouraging: a 4-1 win in Montreal in which the Avalanche took 69% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), their best share of the last five. Brock Nelson has slid into MacKinnon's spot beside Martin Necas and Artturi Lehkonen, Sam Malinski played 24:19 with Makar out, and Lehkonen, who has goals in three straight, now sits on the top line, the top power play and the top penalty kill.

Utah's slide has its own injury list. The Mammoth are winless in six (0-3-3), the last of them a 3-2 home loss to Vancouver, and they are playing without Dylan Guenther, Nick Schmaltz and Nate Schmidt. Vincent Trocheck, in his first season in Utah after the summer trade from the Rangers, has absorbed the extra minutes and is up past 24 a night. Logan Cooley came back Monday after missing two games and is hot in a way the chances support: 14 points in his last ten.

The frustrating part for Utah is that the process has mostly held up. The Mammoth have 58% of the five-on-five expected goals this season, better than Colorado's 53%, and our expected-points count has them level with the Avalanche at 27.4 while the real table says 23 to 27. The gap is in net. Karel Vejmelka is at .869 and -6.3 goals saved above expected, and the Utah coverage this week has been about how much more he needs to give. Mackenzie Blackwood is at .905 and +2.4 for Colorado.

Our numbers see it nearly even, 3.17 expected goals for Colorado to 3.05 for Utah. Colorado's power play (0.84 expected goals a game) against a Utah team that takes 4.7 penalties a night is the matchup to watch, and Trocheck sits one assist from 400 in his career.
headline: Life without MacKinnon and Makar starts in earnest
